$comment: Clause library. Metadata here; prose in text/<id>.txt. Extracted from a sample amendment document with every field restored to a {{Placeholder}} — that document stores cached merge results inline, so a naive text copy would carry a real landlord name, site address, FAN, rent and escalator into every file. Placeholders are named for the ROLE, never the party. The sample used mail merge; this library does not require it — see docs/clause-library.md.

tenantBenefitScale._: How much the TENANT gains from having this clause, as an ask. Signed, because some clauses are things the tenant GIVES. The sign follows one fixed perspective throughout, so scores are comparable across clauses.
tenantBenefitScale.3: Critical. The site is materially exposed without it, or it is the provision landlords most want to restrict.
tenantBenefitScale.2: High. Real value, worth spending negotiating capital on.
tenantBenefitScale.1: Moderate. Worth having, rarely worth a fight.
tenantBenefitScale.0: Neutral. Procedural, or an allocation neither side gains from. ALSO used where the CLAUSE is neutral and the NUMBER is the deal: rent and escalator wrappers score 0 because the comparator prices the figure, and scoring the wrapper as well would count the same advantage twice.
tenantBenefitScale.-1: A concession. The tenant gives something, usually to obtain something else.
tenantBenefitScale.-2: A significant concession, carrying a recurring cost or a long exposure.
tenantBenefitScale._use: Two jobs. In the AUDIT, the gap between what a lease actually contains and what the library scores IS the terms case — a lease missing three +3 clauses is worth pursuing even where the rent is at market. In NEGOTIATION it says what to trade: give a -1 to get a +3.
tenantBenefitScale._caution: A score is a starting point, not an answer. Site-specific facts move it: a rooftop clause scores 0 on a tower, and an interference clause matters far more on a shared site than an exclusive one.

provenance.sample-document: Extracted from the sample amendment document, with cached merge results replaced by placeholders. This language has been used. DEFAULT when the field is absent.
provenance.researched: COMPOSED FROM PUBLISHED MARKET PRACTICE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THAT HAS BEEN USED. These fill gaps the sample did not cover. They are drafting starting points and every one carries status 'draft'. NONE HAS BEEN REVIEWED BY COUNSEL. Do not put one in front of a landlord without review — the risk is not that the language is wrong in the abstract, it is that it may not fit the base lease it is amending.

operations.amend_replace: "Section N of the Agreement is hereby deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following". Use when the base lease has a section that can be cleanly excised. Requires knowing the section number.
operations.amend_include: "The Agreement is hereby amended to include the following terms and conditions". Use when the existing section covers subjects the replacement language does not touch, so deleting it would lose something. Permitted Use is almost always this.
operations.amend_modify: "Section N of the Agreement is hereby amended as follows". A targeted change that leaves the rest of the section standing.
operations.standalone: Adds language that does not reference an existing section.

clauses.title: Access — 24/7, unescorted, no charge, with self-help
clauses.whenToUse: Access governs outage response. The self-help remedy is the part that makes it enforceable — an access right with nothing behind it is a statement of intent.

clauses.title: Boilerplate — authority and no other agreements
clauses.whenToUse: Confirms authority, that the base agreement is in effect, and that no side letters exist. The last of those is the one that earns its place.

clauses.title: Boilerplate — capitalised terms
clauses.whenToUse: Points undefined capitalised terms back at the base agreement. It does NOT rescue a term the base agreement never defined — check the audit before relying on it.

clauses.title: Counterparts and electronic signatures
clauses.whenToUse: Standard, and worth adding to any amendment of a lease predating routine e-signature.

clauses.benefitNote: Excuses performance but expressly not the payment of rent, which is the carve-out landlords check for.
clauses.title: Force majeure
clauses.whenToUse: Standard. Note it excuses performance but expressly not the payment of rent, which is the usual carve-out and the one landlords check for.

clauses.title: Governing law and venue
clauses.whenToUse: Standard. State the jurisdiction explicitly rather than leaving it to conflict-of-laws.

clauses.title: Boilerplate — other terms remain in effect
clauses.whenToUse: Every amendment carries it. Also states which document controls on a conflict, which is the part people leave out.

clauses.title: Severability
clauses.whenToUse: Standard.

clauses.benefitNote: Abatement, temporary facilities and a termination right. Also the standard carve-out from a rent guarantee — the two must agree.
clauses.title: Casualty — rent abatement and termination on damage
clauses.whenToUse: Rooftop sites especially — a fire or structural failure can make the premises unusable while rent keeps running.

clauses.benefitNote: A separate award for equipment, relocation and business interruption, rather than being folded into the landlord's.
clauses.title: Condemnation — termination and separate award
clauses.whenToUse: Ensures Tenant may pursue its own award for relocation and trade fixtures rather than being folded into the Landlord's.

clauses.benefitNote: The usual price of the co-location right. Contingent on a future event, so it does not model as an escalator — price it separately.
clauses.title: Co-location — Landlord share of co-location revenue
clauses.whenToUse: The usual price of a co-location right. 15-30% of the new tenant's rent is a common landlord position.

clauses.title: Co-location — Tenant right to license space to third parties
clauses.whenToUse: Where Tenant owns the structure and wants to host others.

clauses.benefitNote: Mutual and standard.
clauses.title: Compliance — applicable law, FAA and FCC
clauses.whenToUse: Standard, and worth stating where the base lease predates current RF-emission and tower-lighting rules.

clauses.benefitNote: The covenant not to oppose is the operative half. A landlord who signs the application and then objects at the hearing has cost you the site.
clauses.title: Zoning — Landlord cooperation and covenant not to oppose
clauses.whenToUse: Any amendment contemplating a modification that needs a permit. The covenant not to oppose is the operative half — a landlord who signs the application and then objects at the hearing has cost you the site.

clauses.title: Default and cure — periods, with a short cure for access and interference
clauses.whenToUse: The cure period is the margin for an ordinary administrative error. The short period for access and interference is the operative part: those failures take a site off air.

clauses.benefitNote: Protects against pre-existing contamination the tenant did not cause but could be pursued for as an operator.
clauses.title: Environmental — Landlord representation and indemnity
clauses.whenToUse: Protects against pre-existing contamination Tenant did not cause but could be pursued for as an operator.

clauses.benefitNote: A concession, but the generator-fuel and battery carve-out is essential — without it normal site equipment breaches the clause.
clauses.title: Environmental — Tenant obligation, with fuel and battery carve-out
clauses.whenToUse: The reciprocal. The carve-out matters: a generator and its fuel, and battery back-up, are normal site equipment and must not breach a blanket hazardous-materials prohibition.

clauses.title: Escalation — cap the annual increase
clauses.whenToUse: Leaves the existing escalation mechanism in place and puts a ceiling over it. The highest-value escalator clause because it works against an index or a greater-of without having to renegotiate the whole provision.

clauses.title: Escalation — CPI with a floor and a cap
clauses.whenToUse: The trade to offer when a landlord refuses a flat cap: they keep protection against a spike and stop being paid for inflation that did not happen. Name the floor and cap in the amendment.

clauses.title: Escalation — fixed percentage, annually
clauses.whenToUse: The conventional structure. Neutral on its own — what matters is the rate, and whether anything else in the lease also escalates.

clauses.title: Escalation — once per extension term
clauses.whenToUse: Rent steps once every five years instead of every year. Usually cheaper over a long term than an annual escalator at the same headline rate, and easier for a municipal landlord to administer.

clauses.title: Holdover — month to month at the same rent
clauses.whenToUse: Holdover happens because a renewal was missed administratively, not because anyone intended to occupy without a lease. This prices it accordingly.

clauses.benefitNote: Mutual rather than one-way, with a consequential-damages waiver. The waiver is what gets deleted in redlining; watch for it.
clauses.title: Indemnification — mutual, with negligence carve-outs
clauses.whenToUse: Where the base lease indemnity runs one way. Mutual is the defensible position and is easier to sell than a straight deletion.

clauses.benefitNote: Market-standard obligations on the tenant, with mutual waiver of subrogation. Neither side gains.
clauses.title: Insurance — commercial general liability, Landlord as additional insured
clauses.whenToUse: Where the base lease has stale limits. Landlord-side renewals commonly push to update these, so expect it on the table either way.

clauses.benefitNote: Removes the certificate-chasing entirely for a carrier of size.
clauses.title: Insurance — Tenant right to self-insure
clauses.whenToUse: Standard for a carrier of size and worth asking for. Removes the certificate-chasing entirely.

clauses.benefitNote: What makes the covenant enforceable — a 24-hour shutdown, a cure window and injunctive relief. A covenant with no remedy is decorative.
clauses.title: Interference — cure period and remedies
clauses.whenToUse: Makes the interference covenants enforceable by giving them a mechanism: shut down non-emergency operations, cure within a stated period, injunctive relief, then termination.

clauses.benefitNote: A concession, and one worth offering: it makes the protection variant far easier to obtain. Keep it limited to pre-existing users.
clauses.title: Interference — Tenant will not interfere with pre-existing users
clauses.whenToUse: The reciprocal obligation. Expect to concede it; offering it makes the protection variant far easier to obtain.

clauses.benefitNote: Without it the landlord may lease adjacent space to a user who degrades the site, and the remedy is litigation rather than a cure period.
clauses.title: Interference — Landlord will not permit interfering uses
clauses.whenToUse: The core tenant protection on any shared site. Without it, the landlord can lease adjacent space to a user whose emissions degrade the site, and the remedy is a lawsuit rather than a cure period. Pair with the cure-and-terminate variant.

clauses.benefitNote: The landlord lien waiver is the half that matters — equipment stays personal property and stays removable. Lenders ask for it.
clauses.title: Liens — discharge of mechanics liens; Landlord waives lien on Tenant property
clauses.whenToUse: The landlord-lien waiver is the half that matters to Tenant and to any lender: equipment stays Tenant's personal property and remains removable.

clauses.title: Notices — update addresses and method
clauses.whenToUse: Almost always needed and almost always forgotten. A notice sent to a superseded address is a notice not given, and that is how a non-renewal deadline gets missed.

clauses.title: Equipment — modify without consent, with a deemed-approval clock
clauses.whenToUse: Technology refresh cycles are shorter than lease terms. The deemed-approval clock is the part to insist on: without it, consent is a veto exercised by not answering.

clauses.benefitNote: Regularises as-built drift in one clause, where the footprint no longer matches the recorded exhibit.
clauses.title: Premises — exhibit controls over the written description
clauses.whenToUse: Where the premises description is vague or the as-built footprint has drifted from the original exhibit. Attaching a current exhibit and making it control resolves years of ambiguity in one clause.

clauses.benefitNote: Short, standard, and frequently missing from older ground leases.
clauses.title: Quiet Enjoyment — Landlord covenant
clauses.whenToUse: Short, standard, and frequently missing from older ground leases.

clauses.benefitNote: Needed for financing and for any assignment or buyout transaction.
clauses.title: Estoppel certificate — Landlord obligation to deliver
clauses.whenToUse: Needed for financing and for any assignment or lease-buyout transaction.

clauses.benefitNote: Puts third parties on notice without recording the commercial terms.
clauses.title: Memorandum of Amendment — recordable short form
clauses.whenToUse: Puts third parties on notice without recording the commercial terms. Worth doing on any term extension.

clauses.benefitNote: Read this as a bounded concession. If a landlord relocation right is being conceded anyway, this is much better than an unbounded one — an unbounded right is a termination right in disguise. If no such right is on the table, including it gives away something for nothing.
clauses.title: Relocation — permanent relocation only by consent, at Landlord cost
clauses.whenToUse: Where the landlord wants a relocation right. Bound it: comparable location, Tenant's technical approval, Landlord pays, no interruption.

clauses.benefitNote: Reroofing WILL happen across a twenty-year term. This decides whether that means weeks off air and who pays.
clauses.title: Relocation — temporary, for Landlord repair or reroofing, at Landlord cost
clauses.whenToUse: Rooftop sites, and the single most likely operational dispute on one. Reroofing WILL happen during a 20-year term; the question is only who pays and whether the site stays on air.

clauses.benefitNote: Bounds the end-of-term obligation: above-grade only, foundations to a stated depth, and equipment never becomes a fixture.
clauses.title: Removal and restoration — above-grade removal, foundations to depth
clauses.whenToUse: Bounds the end-of-term obligation. The open question in most leases is how far down foundations must come out.

clauses.benefitNote: The notice precondition is the tenant protection: most late payments are address or invoicing failures, not refusals to pay.
clauses.title: Payment — late fee and interest, with notice precondition
clauses.whenToUse: Where the base lease imposes an automatic late fee. The precondition — no fee until written notice and a cure window — is the ask, since most late payments are address or invoicing failures.

clauses.title: Rent — change the amount
clauses.whenToUse: The minimal rent change. Leaves the payment mechanics of the base lease alone, which is what you want when only the number is moving.

clauses.title: Rent — restate amount, escalation and proration
clauses.whenToUse: Where the rent provisions are spread across the chain or the proration treatment is unclear. States the whole economic bargain in one place.

clauses.benefitNote: The defence against lease-buyout aggregators acquiring the rental stream or an easement over the premises.
clauses.title: Right of First Refusal — bona fide offer to purchase the lease or a lease interest
clauses.whenToUse: Defends against lease-buyout aggregators. Gives Tenant the right to match any third-party offer for the rental stream or an easement over the premises.

clauses.benefitNote: Rooftop access is worthless without the route to it. Riser space is the item most often forgotten and the hardest to obtain once it has been let to someone else.
clauses.title: Roof — access route, riser and conduit space
clauses.whenToUse: Rooftop access is worthless without the path to it. Secures the route through the building, riser space for cable, and a place for the ground-level cabinet.

clauses.benefitNote: A restriction on how the tenant may install, but usually the condition that makes a rooftop deal possible at all.
clauses.title: Roof — non-penetrating mounts
clauses.whenToUse: Where the landlord's roof warranty prohibits penetration outright. Ballasted mounts add weight, so this and the structural loading clause interact.

clauses.benefitNote: Removes the two most common rooftop disputes at once: a voided roof warranty and liability for leaks.
clauses.title: Roof — penetrations performed by Landlord's roofer, warranty preserved
clauses.whenToUse: The workable compromise where penetration is unavoidable: Landlord's roofing contractor does the work at Tenant's cost, so the warranty survives and the responsibility question never arises.

clauses.benefitNote: Deemed approval on a supported analysis, and the landlord cannot let another occupant consume the reserved capacity.
clauses.title: Structural — rooftop loading and analysis
clauses.whenToUse: Rooftop sites. Equipment loads can exceed 4,000 lb, so the analysis obligation and the approval standard both need stating.

clauses.benefitNote: Protects the elevation the site was designed around. A forced drop in RAD centre is a coverage loss no rent reduction compensates for.
clauses.title: Structural — reserved tower capacity and RAD centre
clauses.whenToUse: Tower sites. Protects the elevation the site was designed around — a forced drop in RAD centre is a coverage loss that no rent reduction compensates for.

clauses.benefitNote: Lender notice and cure rights. Financing is impractical without it.
clauses.title: Collateral assignment — leasehold mortgage and lender protections
clauses.whenToUse: Where the leasehold is financed. Lenders require notice of default and an opportunity to cure before the lease can be terminated.

clauses.title: Assignment and sublease — affiliates without consent, reasonableness otherwise
clauses.whenToUse: Carrier corporate structures change constantly. The affiliate carve-out is the non-negotiable part; the deemed-consent clock is what stops the rest becoming a veto.

clauses.benefitNote: A real recurring cost. Narrow it to the DOCUMENTED increase attributable to the installation, or it becomes a pass-through of the whole parcel's bill.
clauses.title: Taxes — Tenant reimburses documented increase attributable to its improvements
clauses.whenToUse: The compromise where a landlord demands tax reimbursement. Narrow it to the DOCUMENTED increase ATTRIBUTABLE to the installation, with an assessment showing the allocation.

clauses.benefitNote: A clean allocation rather than an advantage: tenant property, tenant tax.
clauses.title: Taxes — Tenant pays taxes on its own equipment
clauses.whenToUse: Clean allocation: Tenant's personal property is Tenant's, real property is Landlord's.

clauses.title: Term — add four 5-year extension terms
clauses.whenToUse: The existing term is uncontroversial and only the extension structure is being changed. The least disruptive of the three term variants, because it leaves the base term untouched.

clauses.title: Term — replace the remaining option structure
clauses.whenToUse: The existing options are wrong in number, length or mechanism and are being swapped out wholesale. Says so expressly, which matters because a superseded option clause left standing is argued about later.

clauses.title: Term — shorten the non-renewal notice period
clauses.whenToUse: The lease requires a long notice to avoid an automatic renewal. A shorter period is less to remember and less to forfeit. Independent of the other term variants and safe to combine with any of them.

clauses.title: Term — full section restatement (term, extensions, continuation, holdover)
clauses.whenToUse: The tenure provisions are scattered or inconsistent across the chain and it is cleaner to state them once. Maximum control in one clause, and the version to use where the audit found the term ambiguous.

clauses.title: Termination — for convenience, no fee
clauses.whenToUse: The primary termination ask. Use it as the opening position even where a fee is expected to be conceded, because the fee is easier to add than the right is to win.

clauses.title: Termination — for convenience, with a fee
clauses.whenToUse: The usual landing zone where the landlord will not give an unconditional exit. Carve-outs matter more than the fee: without them the fee attaches to terminations for the landlord's own default.

clauses.title: Termination — on landlord default, with self-help
clauses.whenToUse: Pairs with the cure-period clause. The self-help offset is what makes it usable — a termination right alone is a remedy nobody wants to exercise.

clauses.title: Termination — technical or regulatory cause
clauses.whenToUse: Where a convenience right cannot be won at all. Narrower, but the grounds cover most of the reasons a site is actually given up.

clauses.benefitNote: Authority, title, and no encumbrance that would interfere. This is what surfaces an undisclosed mortgage.
clauses.title: Landlord representations — authority, title, no conflicting encumbrance
clauses.whenToUse: On any amendment where ownership has changed since the original, which the document chain will show.

clauses.benefitNote: Subordination without non-disturbance is a trap: a foreclosure would extinguish the lease and the site with it.
clauses.title: SNDA — subordination, non-disturbance and attornment
clauses.whenToUse: Where the property carries a mortgage. Subordination without non-disturbance is a trap: a foreclosure would extinguish the lease and the site with it.

clauses.benefitNote: The right to install back-up power, with testing windows agreed up front rather than disputed monthly.
clauses.title: Generator — installation, fuel storage and testing
clauses.whenToUse: Where back-up power is being added. Landlords raise noise and fuel; agreeing testing windows up front avoids a dispute every month.
